2. The plaintiff-opposite party in a suit for specific performance of contract got a decree on 31. 7. 1977. Against that decree the defendant-petitioner, Mathura Mohan Pandit, preferred First Appeal No. 40 of 1978 in this Division which was decreed in part. The plaintiff Most. Hajera Khatun, after different proceedings started in between the parties which went upto the Appellate Division, put the decree in execution in Title Execution Case No. 2 of 1994 in the Additional Court of Subordinate Judge, Noakhali, which subsequently on transfer to the court of the Subordinate Judge, Lakshmipur was re-numbered as Title Execution Case No. 1 of 1993. During pendency of the said Title Execution Case No. 1 of 1993 the plaintiff filed Miscellaneous Case No. 10 of 1993 in the Court of District Judge, Lakshmipur for transferring the said Title Execution Case to any other competent court. The said transfer petition filed under section 24 CPC was dismissed by the learned District Judge on 10.5.1993. Thereafter the plaintiff-opposite party before me moved an application under section 24 CPC before this Division for transferring the said execution case from the court of Subordinate Judge, Lakshmipur to any other court. Upon such application the following order was passed by Syed Fazle Ahmed, J: 

 "This is an application filed under section 24 CPC read with section 151 of the same for transfer of Execution Case No. 1 of 1993 of the Court of Subordinate Judge, Lakshmipur arising out of Title Suit No. 303 of 1973. 

 The said Title Execution Case No. 1 of 1993 stands withdrawn from the court of Subordinate Judge, Lakshmipur and stands transferred to the court of the learned Subordinate Judge, Noakhali who is competent to try and dispose of the same. The learned Subordinate Judge, Noakhali is directed to dispose of the Title Execution Case No. 1 of 1993 which stands withdrawn from the court of learned Subordinate Judge, Lakshmipur and transferred to the court of Subordinate Judge, Noakhali. 

 Let an order of this court be sent down to the court of Subordinate Judge, Noakhali to dispose of the Execution Case No. 1 of 1993 within the specified time allowed by the court. 

 3. The learned Advocate for the petitioner contends that section 24 CPC provides for hearing of the application for transfer of a case when it is moved before a court. He submits that without-hearing the opposite party-petitioner (the Judgment debtor) the learned Judge in passing the aforesaid order committed serious error of law and the mistake committed calls for review of the order. 

 4. This Rule is resisted by the plaintiff-opposite party on the ground that the execution case having been satisfied the said execution case was not in existence and this Rule shall fail. 

 6. Mr. Dutta put a great stress on the words employed in clause (1) "or for any other sufficient reason." He contends that omission to consider a provision of law is a "sufficient reason" within the meaning of r. 1 of Or. 47 CPC. Mr. Dutta in aid of his submission relied upon the following observation of the Federal Court of India made in the case of Sir Hari Sankar Pal and another vs. Anath Nath Mitter and others reported in 1949 (Fe) 106: ".............................................................................................................................................from such materials as we have got, we are bound to say that in fact there was an omission on the part of the court to consider the clear provision of Order 41 rule 33 when the original judgment was passed: and such omission, which appeared on the face of the judgment, constituted a sufficient ground analogous to those mentioned in Order 47, rule 1 and that therefore the court was not incompetent to reconsider the matter after the judgment if it so desired. 

 7. The aforesaid observation was made in a case where certain property situated in Calcutta City was compulsorily acquired. The said property was leased out to the lessor. In the agreement for lease a clause was inserted relating to the compensation payable for acquisition to the effect that the lessor will get twenty-five times of the rents of the compensation. The property was acquired by the Calcutta Improvement Trust. Compensation being assessed on the interpretation of the clause, an award was made but it was not accepted by the lessor on the ground that the same was not paid in terms of the clause relating to payment of the compensation money. The Calcutta High Court took the view that the clause relates not to the monthly rents spread over the year and allowed the appeal. After the appeal was allowed the decree was made to the tune of twenty-five times of the actual rent. The other non-appealing assignees after passing the decree filed an application under Order 41, rule 33 CPC for modification of the decree seeking for proportionate decree in their favour. The Calcutta High Court granted modification allowing decree in favour of the non-appealing assignees. Against such order of the Calcutta High Court an appeal was taken to the Federal Court of India. In making the aforesaid observation Justice Mukherjee, speaking for the Bench, observed that when there is an omission on the part of a court to take notice of a provision of law an application for review under Or. 47 r. 1 CPC is competent. In this case before me, on perusal of section 24 CPC, I am of the opinion that, where an application for transfer is moved before a court the court is to hear the application after issuance of notice on the other side but where the court suo motu passes an order under this section no notice is required to be given to the other parties. In this case the court without issuing notice on the other parties passed the order sought to be reviewed. This omission to hear the other side is contrary to section 24 CPC and amounts to be some mistake apparent on the face of the record which, in my judgment is covered by the expression for any other sufficient reason employed in r. 1, Or. 47 CPC. 

 8. Mr. Golam Mohiuddin, the learned Advocate who appears in opposing this Rule, informs me that the said execution case in pending before the transferee court at Noakhali. 

 9. Before I part with this judgment it is to be observed that an application for transfer of a case or suit from Subordinate Judge Court to High Court Division or to any Other Court is to be moved before a Division Bench and not before a Single Bench. But in the instant case the order transferring the case has been made by a Single Bench. This is without jurisdiction unless such jurisdiction is given expressly by an order of a learned Chief Justice in accordance with law. From the constitution as given to the Single Bench when the Rule was issued I do not find vesting of such jurisdiction to it. Therefore, on this ground also the review petition is maintainable in the light of the observation made in Sir Hari Sankar Pal and another referred to above in this judgment. Therefore, I have no other alternative but to review the order and re-call the aforesaid Civil Order dated 2.8.1993, passed by SF Ahmed, J.
